public_rationale: A research synthesis publicly available four days before the post identifies poor rare-class performance as a substantial limitation of conventional deep learning. That supports the ordinary reading of a serious practical issue. Existing mitigation methods show progress, so the evidence does not support stronger claims of universal failure or impossibility.
limitations: Evidence is strongest for visual recognition.
Seriousness is qualitative rather than tied to a speaker-specified threshold.
The comparison with reasoning is a description of the targeted methods, not a separately established ranking of all AI approaches.

our_interpretation: The surrounding text identifies the issue as poor handling of rare cases with little training data.
The ordinary reading concerns mainstream data-driven deep learning, not every AI method or an assertion that neural networks cannot reason at all.
Very serious means substantial performance or reliability limitations, not a claim that the problem is impossible to mitigate.
For this continuously reported technical field, current is operationalized as the 2022 state of the art up to the post date, rather than an accounting quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary research documents substantial deficiencies on rare classes or situations in mainstream deep-learning systems, despite stronger performance where training data are plentiful.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary evaluations show that rare-case limitations are generally small or robustly resolved in the relevant methods.

evidence.excerpt: Using conventional methods (e.g., Cross-Entropy loss, or simple fine-tuning, etc.) will result in the poor performance of the tail classes.
evidence.publisher: International Journal of Computer Vision; author manuscript rendered by ar5iv
evidence.explanation: The contemporary synthesis documents poor learning of rare classes and substantial limitations in conventional deep-learning methods. It also reviews mitigation methods, supporting a serious practical problem without implying that every method fails.

evidence.excerpt: Experiments on long-tailed CIFAR, ImageNet, Places, and iNaturalist 2018 manifest the new state-of-the-art for long-tailed recognition.
evidence.explanation: PaCo demonstrates progress on several long-tailed benchmarks using changes within deep learning. This qualifies any stronger interpretation that the problem had no useful mitigation, but does not show it was generally solved in 2022.
